lead.hed: Defense News: Ukraine asks the EU to fund its first PAC-3 Patriot buy
lead.insight: Defense News, Saturday: Kyiv asked to tap a €90 billion EU support loan for PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot batteries — the first formal request to use that loan for the U.S.-made missiles. Because PAC-3s are built in the United States, the purchase needs an exemption from the loan’s non-EU content cap. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the review was moving and that EU representatives were due to decide Monday.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Army photo by Maj. Nicholas Chopp · DVIDS 7275187 · Public domain · A PAC-2 Patriot interceptor launches during a live-fire exercise in Palau, June 15, 2022.

political.hed: USNI: U.S. and Iran trade strikes along the Strait of Hormuz
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: the United States resumed attacking Iranian targets along the Strait of Hormuz this week. Central Command posted video on X saying it hit Iranian targets, including two unidentified ships. The item is a CENTCOM release plus Iranian counter-messaging.

political.hed: Defense News: Air Force speeds a cheaper Reaper successor after Iran losses
political.insight: Defense News, Friday: Lt. Gen. Christopher Niemi said Sept. 3 the Air Force is accelerating a cheaper, more expendable follow-on to the MQ-9A Reaper after combat losses. Officials did not announce a new fielding date. The Massed Modular Aircraft competition is the named path; a fully missionized aircraft is still unpriced.

political.hed: USNI: Chinese destroyer in last summer’s fatal Scarborough collision is back at sea
political.insight: USNI News, Thursday: Type 052D destroyer Guilin (164), involved in a fatal collision with a China Coast Guard cutter at Scarborough Shoal last summer, has returned to frontline service in the South China Sea, according to recent military reports.

tech.hed: NVIDIA agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
tech.insight: NVIDIA, Thursday: the company agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12,930,300,000. CEO Jensen Huang wrote that more than 18 million developers use the hub and that it will stay an open, multi-cloud platform. A signed deal is still a closing process.

tech.hed: AP: Justice Department backs OpenAI against the New York Times on training data
tech.insight: Associated Press: the Trump administration told a court it backs OpenAI’s argument that training on news articles is fair use in the Times copyright case. The brief is a legal position, not a ruling.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: the New Right’s “common good” dresses policy goals in Aristotle
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: “Abusing Aristotle” argues that New Right talk of “the common good” often baptizes contestable industrial-policy aims so they no longer have to survive ordinary cost-benefit argument. Cultural essay, not a statute.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: a predatory state hides behind welfare talk
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: “The Benevolent Smokescreen” argues that extractive governments use social-welfare language to conceal control of production, education, and rents. The piece is political-economy argument, not a U.S. bill.
